# SOP-P1-L3-05 Planned shutdown - Machining line
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, EQ-P1-L3-CN03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-021, ECN-2026-029, ECN-2026-043

Purpose
This procedure defines the approved sequence and controls for a planned shutdown of the machining line at P1-L3 for maintenance, inspection, and changeover activities. It provides background, rationale for critical steps, examples of typical records to keep, and the required approvals to restart.

Scope
Applies to all maintenance technicians, lead operators, and the maintenance planner responsible for EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03 during a planned shutdown event.

Preconditions
1. Work order and shutdown approval completed by maintenance planning and operations.
2. Shift handover has been conducted and the line is in a safe, controlled state.
3. All affected personnel have been notified of the planned shutdown and are present or accounted for.
4. Isolation and lockout/tagout materials are available and inspected for integrity.
5. Permit to work issued for confined space or hot work if required by local rules and related documents ECN-2026-021 and ECN-2026-029 have been reviewed.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
1. Safety footwear and eye protection.
2. Hearing protection where machining noise is present.
3. Thermal protection when working near induction heater components.
4. Gloves and protective clothing appropriate for handling hydraulic fittings and coolant lines.
5. Respiratory protection if fumes or particulates are likely during inspection or cleaning.

Procedure
1. Preparation and safety verification
   1.1. Notify operations control and display shutdown signage at access points.  
   1.2. Verify that all moving parts are stationary and that feed systems are disabled. Lockout/tagout all energy sources to EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03. Rationale: prevents unintentional startup and injury during inspection and maintenance.
   1.3. Confirm isolation of electrical supplies and secure keys with authorized personnel only.

2. Induction billet heater (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) tasks
   2.1. Verify target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Record the last logged process temperature prior to shutdown in the maintenance record. Rationale: ensures there is a documented baseline temperature and avoids thermal shock during service.
   2.2. Allow components to reach a safe handling condition per local thermal procedures before removing covers or sensor housings. Example record: note of thermal state, time last temperature logged, and initials of verifying technician.
   2.3. Inspect coil, water cooling connections, and thermal insulation for damage. Document any anomalies and reference ECN-2026-043 if component replacement is required.

3. Hydraulic forging press (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) tasks
   3.1. De-pressurize hydraulic circuits following equipment isolation. Rationale: prevents hydraulic movement during maintenance.
   3.2. Verify the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 1330 N·m when reassembling ram connections after service. Record torque verification in the maintenance log with the technician’s name. Rationale: correct torque ensures structural integrity and consistent press performance.
   3.3. Inspect ram seals, hoses, and mounting hardware for wear. Keep photographic records of any defects and attach to the work order.

4. CNC machining centers (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) tasks
   4.1. Secure spindle and toolholders. Verify tool inventory and condition. Rationale: prevents tool ejection and maintains part quality after restart.
   4.2. Inspect coolant hoses, filtration, and chip removal systems. Record any filter changes and coolant top-up actions in the service log.
   4.3. Validate axis lubrication points are accessible and that lubricant reservoirs are at acceptable levels per manufacturer guidance. Record lubricant batch reference in maintenance records.

5. Testing and verification prior to restart
   5.1. Remove lockout/tagout only after all technicians have cleared the equipment and tool covers, guards, and access panels are secured.
   5.2. Conduct dry functional checks of safety interlocks and emergency stop circuits.
   5.3. Gradual bring-up procedures: initiate systems per the approved start sequence and confirm nominal conditions are achieved. Document performance checks and any deviations.

Step rationale and examples
- Recording the induction heater setpoint (1235 °C) and the hydraulic ram bolt torque (1330 N·m) provides specific, auditable parameters for thermal stability and mechanical integrity. Example: if a post-maintenance part dimension drift is observed, these recorded values assist root cause analysis.
- Photographic and written records of seal conditions, hose chafing, and insulation damage support warranty claims and engineering change requests referenced in ECN-2026-029 and ECN-2026-043.

Records to keep
- Shutdown work order with signatures.
- Temperature log entries for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 showing the documented target of 1235 °C and last measured values.
- Torque verification entry for EQ-P1-L3-HP02 showing the main ram bolt torque of 1330 N·m and the technician initials.
- Photographs of findings, filter change tags, lubricant batch references, and any replaced parts.
- Post-maintenance test checklist and restart authorization.

Sign-off
1. Maintenance technician: name, signature, date, remarks.
2. Shift supervisor: name, signature, date, confirmation of safe restart readiness.
3. Maintenance planner: name, signature, date, attached records review.
4. Engineering approval if component changes were made, referencing ECN-2026-021, ECN-2026-029, or ECN-2026-043 as applicable.

Notes and references
- Review ECN-2026-021, ECN-2026-029, and ECN-2026-043 for design changes, approved replacement parts, and post-change validation steps.
- Deviations from this SOP require documented risk assessment and explicit approval from maintenance management.
